# Data

**Everything the models see is synthetic and generated by code in this repository.**

Nothing was scraped, purchased or copied from a real counterparty.
Every base rate is marked `[sourced]` or `[assumed]`, and the generative model behind
the labels is published in full.

## 1. What gets generated

| artifact | contents |
|:--|:--|
| `data/generated/deals.parquet` | **2,000 deals** with features, a `deal_went_bad` label and a `train`/`valid`/`test` split |
| `data/generated/evidence/` | **150 labelled evidence bundles** with real PDFs (real text layer) and real PNGs (real pixels) |
| `data/generated/calibration/` | **120 bundles from a different seed (43)**, used only to fit the confidence map |
| `data/generated/counterparties.json` | **30 entities**, 4 of them thin-file |
| `data/fixtures/demo_deal.json` + `demo_evidence/` | the exact demo deal, so [`make demo`](DEMO.md) is reproducible |

### Why the calibration corpus is separate

<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/evaluation-GENUINELY_HELD_OUT-4FD1A5?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">

The confidence map is fitted with isotonic regression on `calibration/`, generated with **seed 43**.
The 150 evaluation bundles in `evidence/` (seed 42) are never touched by fitting, so Suite A is a
genuine held-out measurement rather than **a fit reported as an evaluation**.

Measured for the recorded run: 120 calibration bundles, release rate 0.6417, raw score range
0.0–0.988, class-separable, with anchors `r0 = 0.816167` and `r1 = 0.979`.

**Further reading** &nbsp;
[How confidence is computed and calibrated — ADR-003](DECISIONS.md#adr-003--confidence-is-computed-in-python-then-calibrated-on-a-separate-corpus)

### The documents are real documents

`scripts/docgen.py` renders PDFs with ReportLab (a real text layer that `pypdf` genuinely parses) and
PNGs with Pillow (real pixels, real blur when a scan is meant to be poor). The extraction and
image-analysis paths are therefore actually exercised.

> [!NOTE]
> This matters, and here is the proof that it does: the image analyser originally reported the
> **backdrop** colour as the garment colour. That bug only surfaced because the pixels were real. It
> now extracts a palette and identifies the subject colour by excluding backdrop luma and chroma
> (`BACKDROP_LUMA = 70`, `BACKDROP_CHROMA = 26`).

## 2. Base rates, every one declared

Marked `[sourced]` if it comes from a published figure, `[assumed]` if it is a judgement call.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Every rate below is `[assumed]`. This document says so rather than implying a provenance that does
> not exist.

| constant | value | status | reasoning |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `BASE_DISPUTE_RATE` | **0.11** | `[assumed]` | Deliberately higher than most B2B escrow reporting. A generator that disputes rarely makes the risk model look better than it is. |
| `THIN_FILE_SHARE` | **0.18** | `[assumed]` | The share of counterparties with no completed-deal history. Thin-file cases are where a risk model is most tempted to guess, so they are over-represented rather than under. |
| `ON_TIME_MEAN` | **0.88** | `[assumed]` | Mean on-time delivery rate, σ ≈ 0.09, clipped to `[0.4, 1.0]`. |
| `STRETCH_RISK_KNEE` | **1.5** | `[assumed]` | A deal above 1.5× a seller's largest previous deal is treated as a stretch. The knee is a modelling choice, not an observation. |
| Corpus bad rate | **18.4% train / 18.0% test** | measured | An **output** of the generator below, not an input. |

### The generative model behind `deal_went_bad`

A smooth logistic function of the features, not a lookup table, so the risk model has something real
to learn and the logistic baseline is a fair comparison:

```python
z  = -1.30
z += -0.045 * min(deals_completed, 40)
z +=  2.2   * dispute_rate
z += -1.2   * (on_time_rate - 0.88)
z +=  0.55  * max(0.0, stretch_ratio - 1.5)
z += -1.3   * (objectivity - 0.60)
z += -0.0009 * min(age_days, 1200)
z += -0.06  * (min(milestone_count, 8) - 3)
p  = 1 / (1 + exp(-z))
```

Terms are centred on the corpus means, so the intercept alone sets the base rate.

> [!WARNING]
> **This is published for a reason.** Because the generator is logistic in exactly these features,
> the logistic model is *correctly specified* and the gradient-boosted model has nothing extra to
> exploit — which is why LightGBM loses (test AUC 0.7261 vs 0.7435). That is a property of **this
> corpus**, not evidence that boosting is a bad choice on real data, and the
> [Overview](../README.md#risk-model--reported-not-tuned-away) says so instead of presenting the
> baseline win as a triumph. See
> [ADR-006](DECISIONS.md#adr-006--the-risk-model-is-selected-on-validation-auc-and-the-loser-is-deleted).

### Features the risk model sees

`deals_completed` · `gmv_paise` · `disputes_raised` · `dispute_rate` · `on_time_rate` ·
`largest_deal_paise` · `deal_paise` · `milestone_count` · `counterparty_age_days` ·
`condition_objectivity_score` · `stretch_ratio` · `log_gmv` · `avg_milestone_paise` · `category_code`

`condition_objectivity_score` (mean 0.62, σ 0.2) is the share of clauses that are machine-checkable.
It is a feature because **a deal whose conditions are mostly subjective is genuinely riskier to
automate**, and the demo's top-three factors include it: *"92% of clauses are machine-checkable"*,
factor −0.963.

| split | rows | used for |
|:--|:--|:--|
| train | 1,400 | fitting |
| valid | 300 | hyperparameters **and** the choice between the two models |
| test | 300 | **scored exactly once**, at the end |

## 3. The 150 evaluation bundles

<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/clean-100-4FD1A5?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">
<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/adversarial-50-FFC24B?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">
<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/reported-PER_CATEGORY-C6C0B4?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">

Every adversarial bundle belongs to exactly one category, and every category is reported separately
in [`RESULTS.md`](../backend/evals/out/RESULTS.md) — **an aggregate accuracy can hide a category that
fails completely.**

| category | n | what it tests |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `clean` | 100 | The evidence supports the clause. Releasing is correct. |
| `wrong_date` | 8 | A document dated outside the milestone window. |
| `altered_amount` | 7 | A total edited after issue. |
| `right_type_wrong_milestone` | 7 | A genuine document for a *different* milestone. |
| `fabricated_totals` | 7 | Line items that do not sum to the stated total. |
| `low_quality_scan` | 7 | A genuinely blurred scan — extraction quality drops for real. |
| `photos_cannot_establish_quantity` | 7 | Four photographs cannot evidence a count of 500. **The correct answer is `UNVERIFIABLE` → escalate, not reject.** |
| `valid_but_unusual` | 7 | Odd but legitimate. **Rejecting these is the failure mode.** |

Labels are derived from the **evidence**, following the same published rubric the prose prompt
describes — so a correct pipeline can reach them and an incorrect one cannot be rescued by the label.
The fixture provider has no access to the labels.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `photos_cannot_establish_quantity` and `valid_but_unusual` exist to keep the system honest **in
> both directions**. A system that escalates everything scores well on adversarial cases and is
> worthless; a system that rejects anything unusual punishes honest sellers. Neither failure is
> visible without both categories.

**Further reading** &nbsp;
[The escalation this category produces — Demo minute 3](DEMO.md#minute-3--milestone-02-escalates-and-this-is-the-whole-product) &nbsp;·&nbsp;
[Why it escalates rather than rejects — ADR-004](DECISIONS.md#adr-004--a-required-unverifiable-clause-escalates-it-never-rejects) &nbsp;·&nbsp;
[Per-category accuracy — Overview](../README.md#per-adversarial-category-accuracy)

## 4. Counterparties

30 entities, 4 of them thin-file, spanning `apparel`, `electronics`, `industrial`, `agri`, `services`
and `packaging`. Names, cities and GSTINs are invented. **No real business appears anywhere in this
repository.**

The pricing tier distribution over the 2,000-deal portfolio, measured:

| tier | deals | share | observed bad rate | fee % | hold days | prefund % |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `TIER_1` | 1093 | 54.6% | 4.7% | 0.8 | 0 | 30 |
| `TIER_2` | 338 | 16.9% | 17.5% | 1.5 | 3 | 50 |
| `TIER_3` | 417 | 20.8% | 36.0% | 2.5 | 7 | 100 |
| `DECLINE` | 152 | 7.6% | 67.1% | — | — | — |

The observed bad rate rises **monotonically** with tier, which is the only property that makes the
tiers mean anything. A tier without an explanation is a fee dressed up as a policy — which is why the
[counterparty passport](DEMO.md#if-you-have-one-more-minute) shows the three facts that produced it.

## 5. Personal data

<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/I7-never_on_chain-4FD1A5?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">
<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/I11-never_logged-4FD1A5?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">
<img alt="" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/I12-tenant--scoped_access-4FD1A5?style=flat-square&labelColor=0D0D10">

There is none. Every name, email address, phone number, GSTIN and bank reference in the corpus and
the seed is invented. Demo accounts use `@meridian.demo` and `@tirupur.demo`, which cannot receive
mail.

Artifact bytes are **never logged and never sent on chain**. Access is tenant-scoped through
short-lived HMAC presigned URLs; there is **no public path to an artifact**.

**Further reading** &nbsp;
[Evidence handling — Security §5](SECURITY.md#5-evidence-handling) &nbsp;·&nbsp;
[The masked field list — Security §4](SECURITY.md#4-secrets-and-logging-i11)

---

## 6. Reproducing

```bash
cd backend
uv run python -m scripts.generate_dataset --seed 42   # the corpus
uv run python -m evals.run_all                        # every metric
```

Delete `backend/evals/out/` and re-run: the JSON files are identical apart from timing fields, which
are marked as such in `evals/run_all.py` — `latency_ms`, `wall_ms`, `mean_latency_ms`, `p50`, `p95`,
`max`.

> [!NOTE]
> Determinism here is not a nicety. It is what lets a reader disagree with a number: regenerate the
> corpus, re-run the suites, and compare. Any figure that moved without a seed change is a figure
> worth asking about.
